ruleset: Setting aside, groups and joining a held group are off in new fights (aside 0); pfb_play refuses 'j' / 'h' / 'c' without a held group.
Flip (swap top and bottom edges) is free, unlimited, any piece (flip 1, flip1 0) and does not use the turn.
Your piece need not link (must 0): any free cell where every touching edge fits is legal. It must still TOUCH a piece (pfb_check: 'it has to touch something'); an empty board allows only the centre.
Edge fit is the remaining placement limit: knob in a hole of the same family = fit and link; flat fits anything without linking; wild (blank) fits and links with all; Mud blocks links.

Chains: the placed piece fires, then every linked piece (either side's), in resolve order environment > Guard/Soothe > Trick > Hurt/Charm > Heal/Item; a chain of 3+ uses up every piece that fired (limit).
One action a turn: one placement (or pass). Passing is free (freepass 1).
Hand: every unplayed piece is discarded and a fresh hand of 5 is drawn each round (redraw 1); only Keeper pieces stay; Plenty gives 6.
One shared Yield bar for Hurt and Charm (onebar 1).

The creature's aim (piece and cell) is shown and committed, with its total (aim 1, aimtot 1). Taking its cell or making its edges not fit makes it pick again at full strength; it is not a way to stop damage (aimhit 0: your piece there is not struck).
The creature always links and its aimed piece lands even touching nothing (aimforce).
No free creature spawn piece in new fights (spawn 0).

Already existing player tags: Quick = fires first in its chain (not an extra piece); Heavy = fires last then falls; Trip / Lull = creature skips its next turn; Evade = first hit misses; Hold = guard stays one more turn; Keeper = stays in hand.

Already existing board movers: Wind slides a piece, Water creatures' Current slides one of yours, Tremor knocks pieces off, pal pieces knock off the creature's strongest piece, boss AOE marks break/hurt your pieces there.
Creature Quick = one more piece that turn (creatures only); creature pieces fall after 2 firings (3 for bosses / Guard / Hold).

tiers.10: Light on your feet: ignore a bad edge, nudge your own piece, dodge a hit and drop its piece.
tiers.15: Push and pull: move the creature's aim and its pieces, and plant your own so nothing moves them.
tiers.20: Owning the cell: take a piece back, pull the creature's re-pick beside you, swap places.
tiers.25: Two steps ahead: a second placement, a placement on the creature's turn, a whole knot scattered.
tiers.30: Master of the board: seize the turn order, redraw your layout, decide where the creature lands.

summary: Sidestep teaches the aim cell; every Nimble piece after it is about where and when pieces land, never bigger numbers and never flips or set-aside. Low tiers loosen the one limit left (edge fit) and start moving pieces (yours, then the creature's, then its aim). Capstones buy tempo the rules do not give the player (Double Step, Shadow Step, Call the Tune) or take over the board's layout (Grand Shuffle, Phantom Footing).
question: Should the tempo pieces (Double Step, Shadow Step, Call the Tune) be once a fight, or once a round with a longer Yield bar to keep fight lengths on target?

pieces.name: Long Hop
pieces.text: Leap: it may go on any free cell, even one touching nothing, and a side whose edge does not fit its neighbour is allowed (that side just does not link).
pieces.worth_it: Edge fit is the one placement limit left in v1 (linking is optional, flips are free); Leap is the only piece that ignores it, and the only one that can open a new front far from every piece.
pieces.changes_play: You stop hunting for a cell where all four edges fit: it goes where you need it, beside the Sun, the creature's knot or an empty corner away from a boss mark.
pieces.risk: A mismatched edge could wall off cells. Guard rail: only Leap's own placement ignores fit; later pieces must still fit Leap's edges as usual; a mismatched side never links.
pieces.engine_cost: small: pfb_check skips the 'has to touch' test and treats a non-fitting joint as unlinked for tag leap (player only).
pieces.motif: Edges drawn as springy coils; fire: a hop arc from hand to cell with a dust puff where it lands.
pieces.change_note: A piece need not link today (must 0) and the aim cell almost always touches pieces already, so 'take the aim cell' was free; now Leap also ignores edge fit, the real remaining limit.

pieces.name: Little Nudge
pieces.text: When you place it, slide one of your pieces it touches one cell straight away from it, if that cell is free. Then its chain fires.
pieces.worth_it: The only way for you to move a piece already on the board at tier 10: lift a piece off the boss mark, out of Mud's reach or into a fresh link.
pieces.changes_play: Your board stops being fixed: last turn's piece can be pushed into place to complete a chain this turn.
pieces.risk: Could drag pieces onto the aim cell every turn. Guard rail: one slide, one cell, never off the board or onto a taken cell; moving onto the aim cell just makes it pick again, as today.
pieces.engine_cost: small: the slide in pfb_current (Water's Current) run for your own piece on placement, before pfb_fire.
pieces.motif: Edges as tiny pointing fingers; fire: a gentle elbow-nudge and the touched piece scoots one cell with a scuff line.
pieces.change_note: Turn About gave extra flips; flipping is already free and unlimited (flip1 0).

pieces.name: Skitter
pieces.text: Evade: the creature's next Hurt misses, and the piece that missed tumbles off the board.
pieces.worth_it: A dodge that also clears the board: the missed Hurt cannot fire again or anchor the creature's next chain.
pieces.changes_play: You choose when to let a big Hurt come; the miss costs the creature a board piece, not just a hit.
pieces.risk: Strong against bosses' 3-fire pieces. Guard rail: only the one Hurt that misses; a boss piece loses one firing instead of falling.
pieces.engine_cost: none: existing clauses evade and @miss kill (the miss phase carries the creature piece id, as block does).
pieces.motif: Edges as scuffed footprints; fire: the gnome skitters sideways and the creature's piece skids off the edge.

pieces.name: Wrong Turn
pieces.text: Quick. The creature's aim moves one cell, to the free cell next to it farthest from its own pieces; if its piece does not fit there, it must pick again.
pieces.worth_it: Taking the aim cell today only makes it re-pick its best move; Wrong Turn moves its committed move to a worse cell of your making.
pieces.changes_play: You steer where its next piece lands: away from its links and into your setup (or off the cell you need).
pieces.risk: Can strand the creature over and over. Guard rail: once per round; a bird's second aim is not moved.
pieces.engine_cost: small: new action 'shove' moves foe.plan x/y to a free neighbour (pfb_foe_plan already re-aims when a cell is bad); the aim chip recomputes via pfb_aim_total.
pieces.motif: Edges as a crooked signpost; fire: the aim marker gets spun like a weathervane and hops one cell over.

pieces.name: Elbow Room
pieces.text: When it fires, the creature piece it touches with the highest value slides one cell straight away from it, if that cell is free.
pieces.worth_it: A hit that also unpicks the creature's chain: the shoved piece loses its links before it can fire again.
pieces.changes_play: You break up creature clusters and open cells next to your own pieces.
pieces.risk: Can push pieces off the creature's combos every turn. Guard rail: one push per firing, never onto a taken cell or off the board; the blank never moves.
pieces.engine_cost: small: reuse the Wind slide in pfb_env_fire as action 'shove' for a player piece.
pieces.motif: Edges as bent elbows; fire: a shoulder-barge flash and the creature piece slides with a skid line.

pieces.name: Sure Footing
pieces.text: Hold. While it stands, your pieces touching it (and itself) cannot be moved or knocked off: Current, Wind, Tremor, a Hurt strike and a boss mark pass them by.
pieces.worth_it: The only answer to the board moving your pieces for you: Water creatures, Tremor and boss marks stop wrecking your layout.
pieces.changes_play: You can build a chain inside a boss mark or beside a Tremor and trust it to be there next turn.
pieces.risk: Could make a boss AOE toothless. Guard rail: only pieces touching it; the AOE's 'hurt' and 'heal' kinds still count those pieces; the piece itself fades as normal.
pieces.engine_cost: small: one 'anchored' check in pfb_current, the Wind slide, the Tremor fall list and pfb_aoe_land; 'hold' is the existing tag.
pieces.motif: Edges as stakes driven into soil; fire: the gnome plants its feet and roots curl round the touching pieces.
pieces.change_note: Bundle Up made setting aside free; setting aside is not a v1 mechanic (aside 0).

pieces.name: Step Back
pieces.text: Quick. After its chain, one other piece of yours it linked to that is still on the board goes back to your hand as a Keeper, and its cell is free.
pieces.worth_it: Gets your best Hurt or Guard back for a later placement and opens a cell exactly where you need it.
pieces.changes_play: You rebuild a chain with a better shape, or lift a piece off the creature's aim or a boss mark.
pieces.risk: Loop of re-firing a big piece. Guard rail: once a round; never a piece the chain used up; a piece can be stepped back once a fight.
pieces.engine_cost: medium: new action 'lift' moves a board piece to the hand after pfb_spend and gives it tag keep so the redraw keeps it (hand cap, history snap).
pieces.motif: Edges as a backwards arrow; fire: the linked piece moonwalks off the board into your hand.
pieces.change_note: The whole hand is redrawn each round (redraw 1), so a lifted piece would be discarded before you could play it; it now returns as a Keeper.

pieces.name: Pinning Stance
pieces.text: Hold. While it stands, if the creature has to pick again it may only pick a cell touching this piece; if none fits, it loses that move.
pieces.worth_it: Today a blocked aim just re-picks a move as strong as the old one; Pinning Stance makes the re-pick land where you want it, into your guard and your Riposte.
pieces.changes_play: The aim cell becomes a lever: take it, and the creature's piece is pulled beside your stance (or wasted).
pieces.risk: Lock with Long Hop each turn. Guard rail: at most one lost move per round; the lost piece goes back to its hand, not to waste.
pieces.engine_cost: small: pfb_search for the creature's re-pick filters cells to the stance's neighbours while one of yours stands.
pieces.motif: Edges as planted boots; fire: the gnome stamps, and a pin pops into the aim marker and drags it close.
pieces.change_note: A full 'lost move' on every block clashed with the rule that blocking only reroutes; it now steers the re-pick next to the stance.

pieces.name: Change Partners
pieces.text: When you place it, it swaps places with a creature piece it touches, then the chain fires from the new cell.
pieces.worth_it: Steals a creature cell that links into your chain and drops its piece where it links to nothing.
pieces.changes_play: Reaches the cell you could not fit, and hands the creature a bad spot at the same time.
pieces.risk: Swapping can make illegal edge pairs. Guard rail: only to a cell where both pieces fit; the swapped piece keeps its age and fire count.
pieces.engine_cost: medium: new action 'swap' (cell and x/y exchange plus a fit check) before pfb_fire.
pieces.motif: Edges as linked arms; fire: the two pieces do a little do-si-do and trade cells.

pieces.name: Double Step
pieces.text: After its chain you place one more piece this turn (not another Double Step).
pieces.worth_it: Two placements in one turn: a setup piece and the chain that cashes it in, before the creature answers. Only creatures get this today (their Quick).
pieces.changes_play: Lets you start and finish a chain in one turn, or answer the creature's aim and still attack.
pieces.risk: Biggest tempo swing; shortens fights. Guard rail: once per round; the creature's aim does not change between them.
pieces.engine_cost: medium: a placement counter in pfb_play (one action becomes two for that turn; the creature turn runs after the second).
pieces.motif: Edges as two overlapping footprints; fire: the gnome taps twice and a second hand piece glows ready.
pieces.change_note: Dropped the Quick tag (Quick now means fires first in its chain) and the set-aside group wording; the mechanic is unchanged.

pieces.name: Shadow Step
pieces.text: Keeper. When the creature places its aimed piece, this jumps from your hand onto a free cell touching it and fires there.
pieces.worth_it: A placement on the creature's turn: you answer its move the moment it lands.
pieces.changes_play: You plan around its aim: the guard goes up right as its piece arrives, and your piece now sits in its chain's way.
pieces.risk: A free extra placement each round. Guard rail: it fires alone (no chain) and only if it fits; once a round, then it is used up.
pieces.engine_cost: medium: a reaction hook after the creature's pfb_place; picks the fitting cell with most of your links. Keeper is the existing @hand keep.
pieces.motif: Edges as a dark outline; fire: a shadow pours off the gnome and pops up beside the creature's piece.

pieces.name: Scatter Dance
pieces.text: Cut the creature's hits by {a} this round. Every creature piece touching it slides one cell away from it, where the cell is free.
pieces.worth_it: Clears a whole knot of creature pieces at once; breaks its chains around your piece.
pieces.changes_play: You turn a crowded board into open space for your next chain and leave its pieces stranded.
pieces.risk: Can strip every link a creature has. Guard rail: each piece moves once; nothing fires as they move; never off the board.
pieces.engine_cost: small: soothe:a is an existing clause; 'shoveall' reuses Elbow Room's shove on each neighbour.
pieces.motif: Edges as twirling ribbons; fire: the gnome spins and the creature pieces around it slide outwards like dancers.

pieces.name: Call the Tune
pieces.text: Once a fight. After its chain the creature plays its aim right now; then you place one more piece, and the round ends without another creature turn.
pieces.worth_it: The only way to act both before and after the creature in one round: you see where its piece landed and answer it with a full placement.
pieces.changes_play: Your second piece can chain through its new piece, cut its fresh links, guard the next hit or heal what it just took.
pieces.risk: Turns a round into a free reply. Guard rail: once a fight; your guard from the first placement stays up through its move; the creature still plays (no skip, unlike Trip or Lull).
pieces.engine_cost: medium: run pfb_foe_turn inside your turn, then accept one more placement, then pfb_end_round with no second creature turn.
pieces.motif: Edges as fiddle notes; fire: the gnome plays a reel, the creature dances its move early, and the turn marker swings back to you.
pieces.change_note: Quickstep Reel (the creature skips a turn) duplicated the existing Trip / Lull tags and the 'skip' action.

pieces.name: Grand Shuffle
pieces.text: Move up to three of your pieces on the board to any free cells where they fit. Nothing fires as they move; the next chain finds them.
pieces.worth_it: Redraws your whole board: rescue pieces from Mud, the aim cell, a boss mark or a dead corner and set up one huge chain.
pieces.changes_play: The board stops being fixed: your old pieces become a fresh layout for the next turn.
pieces.risk: Huge puzzle space, slow turns. Guard rail: pieces keep their age and fire count; no piece may move onto the aim cell; three at most.
pieces.engine_cost: large: a multi-step move UI and a check that every moved piece fits.
pieces.motif: Edges as a map grid; fire: the board lifts, three pieces float and settle into new cells.

pieces.name: Phantom Footing
pieces.text: Evade. For the next two rounds you choose where the creature's aimed piece lands: any free cell next to its aim where it fits.
pieces.worth_it: Total control of where its pieces go for two rounds: next to nothing, or into your Riposte setup.
pieces.changes_play: The creature's plan becomes your placement: you build both sides of the board.
pieces.risk: Can strand every creature piece. Guard rail: two rounds, one cell from its aim, only where it fits; if none fits it plays its aim.
pieces.engine_cost: medium: an aim-redirect pick in the player's turn stored on foe.plan, honoured by the creature's placement.
pieces.motif: Edges as misty footprints; fire: the gnome fades, and a ghostly hand slides the creature's aim marker.
